claim: *Audit, Drain, Promote.* A new lint lands audit-only — every finding reported, no commit blocked, so it never breaks an in-flight agent. A fix wave drains it to zero, and only then is it promoted to blocking, so future violations within the mechanism's declared detection surface are refused at that boundary.
topology: Audit-only adoption, iterative fix loop to zero, conditional promotion, one-way regression barrier.
bw_encoding: Black strokes and text; pale gray headers only. Dashed paths retain optional, missing, or forbidden semantics where explicitly labeled. Position, containment, line weight, and written labels carry distinctions without color.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames. Final QA: explicit panel-caption line breaks, clear promotion label placement, or increased history-step gaps as applicable.
alt: A new smell-detecting lint moves through three states, left to right. First it lands audit-only: it reports every finding but blocks no commit, so it never breaks an in-flight agent. Then a fix wave — an agent making behavior-preserving edits under test coverage — drains the finding count to zero; this is drawn as a loop beneath the Findings to zero box and runs while the lint remains audit-only until nothing is left. Only when the count reaches zero is the lint promoted to blocking: it now fails any commit that reintroduces the smell. A one-way barrier sits after the blocking state, marking that the class of smell can never return. Squash the findings, drive them to zero, then promote — and the smells that leave stay gone.
